s: Who was the Chief Justice of India when public interest litigation (PIL) was introduced to the Indian Judicial System?
x: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) emerged in the late 1970s and early 1980s as a tool to make justice accessible to the poor and marginalised. Justice P.N. Bhagwati, along with Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer, played a pioneering role in liberalising the concept of locus standi. During his tenure as Chief Justice of India (1985–1986), PIL became firmly institutionalised in the Indian judicial system.

s: ‘Judicial Activism’ in India is related to –
x: Judicial Activism in India is related to Public Interest Litigation. Judicial Activism in India started in the mid 1970s, on the initiative of the Supreme Court.

s: Who was the Chief Justice of India when Public Interest litigation was introduced in the Indian Judicial System?
x: The concept of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) agrees with the principles enshrined in Article 39A of the Constitution of India to protect and deliver prompt Social Justice with the help of law. Before the 1980s, only the aggrieved party could approach the Courts for justice. After the Emergency era, the Supreme Court reached out to the people, devising a means for any person of the public (or an NGO) to approach the court seeking legal remedy in cases where the public interest is at stake. Justice P. N. Bhagwati and Justice V. R. Krishna Iyer were among the first Judges to admit PILs in court. PIL can be filed both in the High Courts and the Supreme Court.

s: Where can the Public Interest Litigation (PIL) be filed?
o: Only in Supreme Court of India
Only in High Courts of States
Both in High Courts & Supreme Court
x: PIL can be filed under Art. 32 in the Supreme Court or Art. 226 in the High Courts, so option 4 is correct. Tribunals like the CAT are not the forum for PIL.

s: The concept of PIL originated in which of the following countries?
x: PIL and judicial activism originated in the USA (the term was coined there in 1947), and India adopted PIL in the late 1970s. England, Russia and China are therefore wrong.
